title: The derived completion is complete with the same reductions
statement:
For every $M\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, the derived completion
$\widehat M=R\varprojlim\operatorname{red}(M)$ of [det-pbc-complete-towers] is
derived $\pi_E$-complete, and the completion map
$\kappa_M\colon M\to\widehat M$ induces an isomorphism
$\operatorname{red}(\kappa_M)\colon\operatorname{red}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{red}(\widehat M)$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$; in particular
$M_m\simeq\widehat M_m$ for every $m\geq1$.

proof.text:
Fix $m$ and put $R_m=[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^m}\mathcal O_{E,T}]$, so that
$\operatorname{red}(N)_m=N\otimes R_m$ ([det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]). By
[det-pbc-complete-tower-calculus] (5),

$$
\widehat M\otimes R_m\simeq R\varprojlim_n\bigl(M\otimes R_n\otimes R_m\bigr).
$$

For $n\geq m$ the complex $R_n\otimes R_m$ is quasi-isomorphic, compatibly with
the transitions in $n$, to $R_n\otimes(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T=
[(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T\xrightarrow{0}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T]$, which is the
direct sum of $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T$ in degree $0$, with identity
transitions, and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T[1]$, with transitions multiplication
by $\pi_E$ (the degree $-1$ component of the transition maps of
[det-pbc-complete-towers] (3)). Hence the tower $(M\otimes R_n\otimes R_m)_{n\geq m}$
is the direct sum of the constant tower $c(M_m)$ and a tower $N_\bullet$ in
which every composite of $m$ transitions is multiplication by $\pi_E^m$, which
is zero on $M_m$. For $N_\bullet$ the endomorphism $T$ of $\prod_nN_n$ in the
Milnor cone satisfies $T^m=0$, so $1-T$ is invertible with inverse
$\sum_{k<m}T^k$, and $R\varprojlim N_\bullet=0$. Finitely many levels $n<m$ do
not change the derived limit. Therefore $\widehat M\otimes R_m\simeq
R\varprojlim c(M_m)\simeq M_m$, and this isomorphism is inverse to
$\kappa_M\otimes R_m$, since $\kappa_M\otimes R_m$ is induced by the inclusion of
the constant summand. The identifications are compatible with $m+1\to m$, which
gives the isomorphism of towers $\operatorname{red}(\kappa_M)$ (an isomorphism
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$ by [det-pbc-complete-tower-calculus] (2)).

Completeness of $\widehat M$. The same computation with the roles of $n$ and
$m$ exchanged shows that, for fixed $n$, the complex $N_n=M\otimes R_n$ is
derived complete: for $m\geq n$, $R_m\otimes R_n\simeq
[(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T\xrightarrow{0}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T]$ compatibly with
the transitions in $m$, so $(N_n\otimes R_m)_m$ is the sum of the constant tower
$c(N_n)$ and a tower whose $n$-fold composites of transitions vanish, and
$\kappa_{N_n}\colon N_n\to R\varprojlim_m(N_n\otimes R_m)$ is an isomorphism. Now
$\widehat M=R\varprojlim_nN_n$, and by [det-pbc-complete-tower-calculus] (5)

$$
\widehat{\widehat M}=R\varprojlim_m\Bigl(\bigl(R\varprojlim_nN_n\bigr)\otimes R_m\Bigr)
\simeq R\varprojlim_mR\varprojlim_n(N_n\otimes R_m)
\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\varprojlim_m(N_n\otimes R_m),
$$

the last step because both iterated Milnor cones are the total complex of the
commutative square formed by $1-T_n$ and $1-T_m$ on
$\prod_{n,m}N_n\otimes R_m$. Under these identifications
$\kappa_{\widehat M}=R\varprojlim_n\kappa_{N_n}$, since both are induced by the
inclusions of the constant towers. Each $\kappa_{N_n}$ is an isomorphism, hence
so is $\kappa_{\widehat M}$, and $\widehat M$ is derived complete
([sk-def-pe-derived-completion]).

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and for a scheme $T$
write $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and
$(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$ for the pulled-back coefficient rings
([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]), and
$D(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ for the derived category of
$\mathcal O_{E,T}$-modules.

*Notation.*

1. *Towers.* $\operatorname{Tow}(T)$ is the abelian category of towers
   $M_\bullet=(M_n,t_n\colon M_{n+1}\to M_n)_{n\geq1}$ of
   $\mathcal O_{E,T}$-module sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$, with levelwise
   morphisms. Write
   $\operatorname{ev}_n\colon\operatorname{Tow}(T)\to\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}$ for
   evaluation at level $n$, $c\colon\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}\to\operatorname{Tow}(T)$
   for the constant tower with identity transitions, and
   $\varprojlim\colon\operatorname{Tow}(T)\to\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}$ for the
   limit, right adjoint to $c$. The *derived limit*
   $R\varprojlim\colon D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))\to D(T)$ is the right derived
   functor of $\varprojlim$; on a tower of complexes it is the Milnor cone
   $\operatorname{Cone}(\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nM_n)[-1]$, a derived
   limit of $(\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet)_n$ in the sense of
   [def-weil-derived-limit].
2. *Levelwise functors.* For a morphism of schemes $u\colon T'\to T$, the module
   pullback and pushforward of [det-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], applied
   levelwise, give $u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}\colon\operatorname{Tow}(T)\to
   \operatorname{Tow}(T')$ and $u_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}\colon
   \operatorname{Tow}(T')\to\operatorname{Tow}(T)$, with
   $u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}\dashv u_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. Write
   $Ru_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ for the right derived functor of
   $u_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$; $u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ is exact and needs no
   deriving.
3. *Reduction tower.* For a complex $M$ of $\mathcal O_{E,T}$-modules let

   $$
   \operatorname{red}(M)_n=\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(M\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}M\bigr)
   =M\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}],
   $$

   with transitions induced by the map of resolutions
   $[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^{n+1}}\mathcal O_{E,T}]\to
   [\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}]$ equal to $\pi_E$ in
   degree $-1$ and the identity in degree $0$, which lifts
   $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_T\to(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$. By
   [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution],
   $\operatorname{red}(M)_n\simeq M_n=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}
   (\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$. The construction is functorial on complexes,
   commutes with cones and preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so it defines an exact
   functor $\operatorname{red}\colon D(T)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$, the
   *reduction tower*.
4. *Completion map.* The inclusions of $M$ in degree $0$ of the cones give a
   morphism of towers $c(M)\to\operatorname{red}(M)$; applying $R\varprojlim$ and
   using $R\varprojlim c(M)\simeq M$ gives the *completion map*

   $$
   \kappa_M\colon M\longrightarrow\widehat M:=R\varprojlim\operatorname{red}(M),
   $$

   natural in $M$. It is the canonical map of [def-pe-derived-complete], so $M$
   is derived complete if and only if $\kappa_M$ is an isomorphism.
   $\widehat M$ is the *derived completion* of $M$.

*Assertions.* Let $u\colon T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes.

1. $\operatorname{Tow}(T)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category. Each
   $\operatorname{ev}_n$ is exact and has an exact left adjoint, so it carries
   K-injective complexes of towers to K-injective complexes of modules.
2. A morphism $a$ of $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$ is an isomorphism if and only if
   $\operatorname{ev}_n(a)$ is an isomorphism in $D(T)$ for every $n$.
3. $\operatorname{ev}_n\circ u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}=u^*\circ\operatorname{ev}_n$ and
   $\operatorname{ev}_n\circ Ru^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*\simeq Ru_*\circ\operatorname{ev}_n$,
   compatibly with the units and counits of $u^*\dashv Ru_*$
   ([def-weil-derived-direct-image]) and
   $u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}\dashv Ru^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*$.
4. There is a canonical isomorphism
   $Ru_*\circ R\varprojlim\simeq R\varprojlim\circ Ru_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ of
   functors $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T'))\to D(T)$.
5. $R\varprojlim$ is exact. For an exact equivalence
   $F\colon\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}\to\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T'}}$, applied levelwise
   as $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, one has $F\circ R\varprojlim\simeq
   R\varprojlim\circ F^{\operatorname{Tow}}$; and
   $R\varprojlim(M_\bullet)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}P\simeq
   R\varprojlim(M_\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}P)$ for every bounded complex
   $P$ of finite free $\mathcal O_{E,T}$-modules.
6. For every $M\in D(T)$ the derived completion $\widehat M$ is derived
   complete, and $\kappa_M$ induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{red}(\kappa_M)\colon\operatorname{red}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}
   \operatorname{red}(\widehat M)$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$; in particular
   $M_m\simeq\widehat M_m$ for every $m\geq1$.

proof.text:
(1) $\operatorname{Tow}(T)$ is the category of functors from the poset
$\mathbf Z_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the Grothendieck abelian category
$\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}$, hence Grothendieck abelian, with limits, colimits and
exactness computed levelwise. The left adjoint of $\operatorname{ev}_n$ sends
$N$ to the tower equal to $N$ in levels $m\leq n$, with identity transitions
there, and to $0$ in levels $m>n$; it is exact. A right adjoint of a functor
with an exact left adjoint preserves K-injective complexes:
$\operatorname{Hom}(B,\operatorname{ev}_nI)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_nB,I)$ is acyclic
for acyclic $B$.

(2) Cohomology in $\operatorname{Tow}(T)$ is computed levelwise, so a complex of
towers is acyclic if and only if each level is. Apply this to the cone of a
representative of $a$.

(3) The first equality holds on the nose. For the second, compute
$Ru^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*$ by a K-injective complex of towers $I_\bullet$; by
(1) each $\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet$ is K-injective, so
$\operatorname{ev}_nu^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*I_\bullet=u_*\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet$
computes $Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet$ ([def-weil-derived-direct-image]).
Units and counits are defined levelwise, so they are compatible.

(4) The functor $u^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*$ is right adjoint to the exact functor
$u^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ ([det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], levelwise), and
$\varprojlim$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $c$; hence both preserve
K-injective complexes, by the argument of (1). Therefore
$R\varprojlim\circ Ru^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*=R(\varprojlim\circ u^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*)$
and $Ru_*\circ R\varprojlim=R(u_*\circ\varprojlim)$. The underived functors agree,
$\varprojlim\circ u^{\operatorname{Tow}}_*=u_*\circ\varprojlim$, because $u_*$
commutes with limits; this gives the isomorphism.

(5) Countable products in $\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}$ are exact ([det-pe-products-exact]), so
$R\varprojlim$ is computed on any tower of complexes by the Milnor cone
([det-pe-milnor-sequence]), which agrees with the K-injective computation by
[lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (3). The Milnor cone is built from a
product and a cone. An exact equivalence preserves products and cones. For a
bounded complex $P$ of finite free modules, $-\otimes P$ is a finite iterated
cone of finite direct sums of shifts of the identity, applied termwise, so it
commutes with $\prod_n$ and with the cone of $1-T$.

(6) Fix $m$ and put $R_m=[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^m}\mathcal O_{E,T}]$, so that
$\operatorname{red}(N)_m=N\otimes R_m$ ([det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]). By (5),

$$
\widehat M\otimes R_m\simeq R\varprojlim_n\bigl(M\otimes R_n\otimes R_m\bigr).
$$

For $n\geq m$ the complex $R_n\otimes R_m$ is quasi-isomorphic, compatibly with
the transitions in $n$, to $R_n\otimes(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T=
[(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T\xrightarrow{0}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T]$, which is the
direct sum of $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T$ in degree $0$, with identity
transitions, and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_T[1]$, with transitions multiplication
by $\pi_E$ (the degree $-1$ component of the transition maps of notation 3).
Hence the tower $(M\otimes R_n\otimes R_m)_{n\geq m}$
is the direct sum of the constant tower $c(M_m)$ and a tower $N_\bullet$ in
which every composite of $m$ transitions is multiplication by $\pi_E^m$, which
is zero on $M_m$. For $N_\bullet$ the endomorphism $T$ of $\prod_nN_n$ in the
Milnor cone satisfies $T^m=0$, so $1-T$ is invertible with inverse
$\sum_{k<m}T^k$, and $R\varprojlim N_\bullet=0$. Finitely many levels $n<m$ do
not change the derived limit. Therefore $\widehat M\otimes R_m\simeq
R\varprojlim c(M_m)\simeq M_m$, and this isomorphism is inverse to
$\kappa_M\otimes R_m$, since $\kappa_M\otimes R_m$ is induced by the inclusion of
the constant summand. The identifications are compatible with $m+1\to m$, which
gives the isomorphism of towers $\operatorname{red}(\kappa_M)$ (an isomorphism
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T))$ by (2)).

Completeness of $\widehat M$. The same computation with the roles of $n$ and
$m$ exchanged shows that, for fixed $n$, the complex $N_n=M\otimes R_n$ is
derived complete: for $m\geq n$, $R_m\otimes R_n\simeq

the transitions in $m$, so $(N_n\otimes R_m)_m$ is the sum of the constant tower
$c(N_n)$ and a tower whose $n$-fold composites of transitions vanish, and
$\kappa_{N_n}\colon N_n\to R\varprojlim_m(N_n\otimes R_m)$ is an isomorphism. Now
$\widehat M=R\varprojlim_nN_n$, and by (5)

$$
\widehat{\widehat M}=R\varprojlim_m\Bigl(\bigl(R\varprojlim_nN_n\bigr)\otimes R_m\Bigr)
\simeq R\varprojlim_mR\varprojlim_n(N_n\otimes R_m)
\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\varprojlim_m(N_n\otimes R_m),
$$

the last step because both iterated Milnor cones are the total complex of the
commutative square formed by $1-T_n$ and $1-T_m$ on
$\prod_{n,m}N_n\otimes R_m$. Under these identifications
$\kappa_{\widehat M}=R\varprojlim_n\kappa_{N_n}$, since both are induced by the
inclusions of the constant towers. Each $\kappa_{N_n}$ is an isomorphism, hence
so is $\kappa_{\widehat M}$, and $\widehat M$ is derived complete
([def-pe-derived-complete]).
